2.text: Being upright smacks of effort, you opt to be horizontal - a solid first move.

3.text: You think you'll have just one more day in bed before you start being production - adorable!

4.text: A friend reminds you that groceries can be delivered. You order them. You will not eat them.

5.text: You leave the hospital bubble and get a cold. You used to think this was what 'very poorly' meant. You know better now.

6.text: You think about showering, dressing, shopping, cooking - these remain bizzarely abstract concepts.

7.text: Deeply resentful at having to sort your own medication.

8.text: You open the inbox you haven't dealt with for 3 months. Not today either!

9.text: You have to sit on the floor to stop the kitchen spinning while the kettle boils.

10.text: You are both ravenous and repulsed by most foods.

11.text: You haven't slept properly yet. You worry you are failing at recovery.

12.text: You feel nostalgia for your favourite nurses.

13.text: You emerge from your duvet cocoon, furious at needing to fulfil your responsibilities.

14.text: You get a haircut and feel less like a feral hospital goblin.

15.text: You shave your legs without falling over. Orthostatic what now? You celebrate ... prematurely.

16.text: You stand chatting in the park for 10 minutes and feel nauseous, sweaty, and faint - you beat a glacial retreat.

17.text: You tweak the shoulder you strained in hospital. Holding a cup of tea is now a Herculean task.

18.text: Sulk because there is no one to bring you snacks.

19.text: Go to the theatre, manage all the steps, feel absurdly proud of yourself.

20.text: Today we sleep. Existentially, you are a deflated marshmallow.

21.text: You restart an interrupted work project. You last half an hour before going back to bed.

22.text:
Feel bad.
Eat.
Feel better.
Surprise!

23.text: You find leftover hospital snacks in the fridge and have a full body shudder of revulsion.

24.text: Walk a quarter of a mile feeling dizzy the whole way. Will do it again tomorrow. Worst hoby EVER!

25.text: You're cold, you put on a jersey. You are now hotter than the earth's molten core.

26.text: Blow your hospital energy budget on an ontologically rejuvenating Caper. No regrets, but you still cry outside the pharmacy.

27.text:
You stood up.
That's your quota for today.
Lie down.

28.text: You read 2,000 pages of medical notes and find 4 things of interest. World's most boring novel. Zero stars.

29.text: You cry because your food delivery is delayed.

30.text: You journal your experiences - you call them 'The Shit Fit Chronicles'

31.text: A friend asks how you're doing - you give them a blow-by-blow account - you can never speak to them again.

32.text: The NHS correspondence pile is bigger than your pension plan.

33.text: Walk to Greggs for fresh air, drop your steak bake and knock over your coffee. Fresh air is for losers.

34.text: You realise the hospital energy budget was a figment of your imagination.

35.text: You buy more groceries you are too tired to prepare and will throw out.

37.text: The Deliveroo man doesn't know your name, but he knows your secret code.

38.text: Someone makes a decision for you, not with you. Autonomy Override Alert activated.

39.text: You drop something on the floor, decide you never really needed it. It lives there now.

40.text:
Your brain is
in cosmic inflation, your body hasn't been outside for 3 days.

41.text: You cry because you are cold and your jersey is beyond arm's reach.

43.text: You roll over in bed. Everything pops like bubble wrap.

44.text: Your arm hurts and you don't know why? It's your phantom PICC line.

45.text: Though precedes action. You think about tidying. Action TBD.

46.text: Your calves feel swollen. You Google compartment syndrome and ruminate on lower leg amputation. You take a nap.

47.text: You cry because you are awake + PAIN.

48.text: Your bestie comes to visit, stays in an hotel, cleans your house while you watch, and leaves early. You LOVE her!

49.text: You skip a work meeting because work is DUMB. New levels of self-advocacy and petulance unlock simultaneously.

50.text: You scroll for an hour before getting out of bed, then realise you're worn out and need a nap.

51.text: You book next week's gym sessions. Next Week You cancels all of them.

52.text: Someone tries to tell your story for you. You correct the narrative. Authorial Integrity retained.

53.text: You coin the term 'pus ferrets' to describe your drains and laugh until you cry. Core workout completed.

54.text: You insist you can do something. You cannot. The only person surprise is YOU.

55.text: You forget the real world is not hospital and go to Sainsbury's in your pyjamas.

56.text: You indulge your nerdery at a lecture and walk up 8 flights of stairs in the carpark without the handrail. You sing 'Eye of the Tiger' and shadow box with glee.

57.text: You used up a week's worth of energy posing at a lecture and parking on the 8th floor. Hubris, pure hubris.

58.text: Your empty pill box is a violation of your civil liberties.

59.text: Sleep. Wake. Snack. Sleep. It is what it is - this is what they mean by Zen.

60.text: Put clothes in the washing machine. They are now trapped in an infinity wash for 7 - 10 business days.

61.text: Your legs burn like fire ants have taken up residence in your epidermis.

62.text: You do 2 minutes on the rowing machine and feel 25 again. You sleep for the rest of the day - in your gym clothes.

63.text: Accept that your usual 6am start time is now 10am.

64.text: You buy another bottle of coke you can't open. A random passerby has to do it for you.

65.text: Check credit card statement - you've spent a month's salary on Just Eat. Feel depressed, order a burger.

66.text: You are dizzy standing up. You sit down. You are dizzy sitting down. You go to bed.

67.text: More groceries? You indefatigable optimist! You put another bin liner in, because ... well ...

68.text: Spend 5 hours on the sofa listening to your tinnitus with a cup of tea.

70.text: You tell your 100th person 'I'm not very good at stairs at the moment'.

71.text: Too tired to shower. Too filthy not to.

72.text: You turn on your desk light and feel like you're being interrogated by the Stasi.

73.text: You try to be helpful. You are not. You have created more work.

74.text: NHS text reminders drive you bonkers, even though you still need them.

75.text: Your irritation at the term 'early convalescence' becomes reluctant acknowledgement that it's 'a thing' and you're doing it.

76.text: You mistake a long drive for a low-effort activity. Your small pain will now become BIG PAIN for at least 7 days.

77.text: You try to rate your pain but it involves the Fibonacci sequence.

78.text: You wear an actual outfit with accessories and perfume. You are back in your pyjamas by 3pm, but at least you smell good.

79.text:
You eat an 'extended-family'
sized bar of chocolate. You would have preferred vegetables.

80.text: You are an obnoxious baby in physio. you cry, you eat, you sleep, you are filled with regret + PAIN.

81.text: You think 'maybe I'll go out today', the **Gods of Convalescence** laugh at your plans.

82.text: Your body temperature is now in Cryogenic Mode. Walt Disney is your new neighbour.

83.text: You try to salute a stupid driver and realise your middle finger is now in the target audience for Viagra.

84.text: You cry because ... honestly ... you forget why.

85.text: You spontaneously load and unload the dishwasher in the same 24 hour period. Heroic.

86.text: You buy groceries, cook them, and clean up all in the same hour. You nap to celebrate.

87.text: You felt great for two days in a row - have some crushing fatigure ... and PAIN.

88.text: Walking pace: geriatric tortoise on sedatives.

89.text: You finally understand that convalescence is a pattern of stable chaos. Your bed is the attractor.

90.text: Kitchen noises are a physical assault. You are filled with murderous noise-fuelled rage.

91.text: Can solve for 'x', cannot put away laundry.

92.text: You can sign your own name again, but the electrical storm in your hand is ongoing.

93.text: Your new love of steak bakes is a culinary violation of everything you stand for - you eat another one anyway.

94.text: Your carpet is an affront to decency, but the vacuum cleaner weighs more than a whale.

96.text: You have a day with no pain. You think you are cured - you are not.

97.text: You play the 'I nearly died' card with your brother during a vicious round of Uno - he plays the +5 card.

98.text: An acquaintance wants to visit. It's easier to unfriend them than tidy the house.

99.text: You compare weight loss wattles with a colleague on Ozempic. You're winning.

100.text: 'Early convalescence' is over. Advance to new levels of existential bullshit.
